newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Die Erste leaves open Creditanstalt ambitions.
newsitem.headline: Die Erste leaves open Creditanstalt ambitions.

text.p: Austrian savings bank Die Erste on Monday said it was still eyeing a role in the race for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt, ten days after leaving a last-ditch Austro-Italian-German group of bidders for the bank.

"As long as the finance minister's decision is still open, this topic isn't finished for us," chief executive Konrad Fuchs told journalists. "We're waiting for his decision and then we'll re-evaluate the situation."

Die Erste, Austria's oldest savings bank, on September 6 left a consortium that has made the only known bid for the government's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt after hectic last-minute talks failed to produce agreement on the terms of a joint offer.
The consortium is led by Austro-Italian insurer EA-Generali and includes Commerzbank of Germany and Banca Commerciale Italiana.

Finance Minister Viktor Klima, in charge of the sale, has hinted he is less than happy with the offer, which reportedly is for half the state's 19.9 million shares in the bank and proposes to place the rest in a secondary offering.
The government has repeatedly said it wants to sell its entire stake for cash, eager for up to 18 billion schillings ($1.7 billion) in projected revenue to plug its growing budget holes.
Klima's final decision whether to accept the group's bid or reopen the race to other potential buyers is not expected before the end of the week.
